unsupported_claims: Summary claim that 'the entire 16% gap is the 8-entry centroid constant-memory LUT' is contradicted by the same doc's own isolation test: docs/experiment-decode-speed.md reports the constant-centroid ceiling at 78.1 tok/s (1.00x) but the index-only (no LUT, bit-extraction still live) test at 70.1 tok/s (0.90x of q8_0) at 8K. Bit extraction therefore accounts for ~10.9 points of the 18.5-point gap and the LUT only the remainder; the headline overstates and the reading repeats it while also reporting the contradicting 70.1 number.

Claim that the two prefill stories are 'unreconciled in-tree' / 'not reconciled in-tree' is overstated: branch README.md line 57 explicitly reconciles them ('the final number (2524 at 4K) is lower than the peak (2747 at 512) because longer context is naturally slower; the key metric is the ratio'). The two rows are also different context lengths, so the juxtaposition is apples-to-oranges rather than a contradiction.

The claim that context-scaling-fix's commits touch '.github/workflows/ci.yml' is false. `git diff --name-only b8c4650..367bb2d -- .github/` is empty and commit eed5a63 changes only scripts/turbo-quality-gate.sh. The 15 commits touch 9 files: README.md, 7 docs, scripts/turbo-quality-gate.sh.

'141 pytest tests, 95% coverage gate' merges two inconsistent source claims without flagging: README.md lines 13/209/223 claim 141 tests and 100% coverage, while .github/workflows/ci.yml sets --cov-fail-under=95. Static count at the branch tip is 99 `def test` functions (parametrization could raise the collected count, but 141 was not verified).

'context-scaling-fix's first unique commit is bd3b403' is misleading: the branch is fully merged into main (`git log main..experiment/context-scaling-fix` is empty, merge-base = 367bb2d), so it has no unique commits vs main; bd3b403 is simply a mid-branch commit whose parent is b8c4650.

The unixsysdev '-0.8% speed loss at block-32' is presented next to '0.622x prefill / 0.385x decode'. The -0.8% note in docs/turbo-speed-investigation.md line 247 states no baseline and is almost certainly relative to its own block-128, not q8_0; juxtaposing it with the vs-q8_0 matrix figure is misleading.
errors_found: Decode-at-8K is reported as both 0.84x (65.4/78.3) and 0.76x (59.2/77.7) within the same reading. docs/experiment-decode-speed.md is itself internally inconsistent (its 'Regression Against Main' table gives main 65.8 vs branch 61.5), and the reading reproduces both numbers without flagging the contradiction.

Internal contradiction: the summary says 'The KV-cache code is NOT here' while reusable_assets lists turboquant/kv_cache.py on the branch tip. The C++/Metal kernels are in the separate fork; the Python reference is in this repo.

'decode-speed-parity adds 3 docs' is true only relative to 367bb2d; relative to main its base commit b4fa8b6 (which adds docs/turboquant-plus-experiments.md) is already on main, so `git diff --stat $(git merge-base experiment/decode-speed-parity main)..experiment/decode-speed-parity` shows only 2 docs. The reading's own merge-base fact conflicts with the 3-doc claim.

The 141-test figure is sourced from a branch tip dated 2026-03-25 that is ~6 months stale vs main@2026-07-20; current main collects 354 tests (with 11 collection errors in this environment). The reading presents the branch README's count as the test surface without dating it.

'All three branches are DOCS-ONLY relative to their fork point' is true, but the reading then lists the Python implementation as a branch-tip reusable asset without noting it is inherited unchanged from the base commit (the experiment commits add no Python).

Minor: key_fact 3 says 'decode-speed-parity@2461b26 is NOT an ancestor of main' (true for the tip) but the summary says it 'forks from 367bb2d'; its merge-base with main is b4fa8b6, so the branch is main + 8 commits, not a clean fork from 367bb2d.
missing_angles: main contains docs/papers/dflash-self-draft-investigation.md, a 31-experiment speculative-decoding study that finds a ~1.33x theoretical speedup ceiling on 75%-GDN hybrid architectures and that training DFlash drafts from scratch on consumer hardware (M5 Max) is not feasible. The reading's seed 4 (tiny draft sharing the turbo3 KV cache) is directly constrained/pre-empted by this in-tree paper, which the reader never opens.

main carries ~16 papers directly on the town's KV-compression thread (why-mse-fails-for-kv-quantization.md, block-size-experiment.md, layer-aware-v-compression.md, sparse-v-dequant.md, moe-v-compression-frontier.md, longctx-1m-and-triattention.md, block-selector-sparse-attention.md, etc.); the reading reads only docs/benchmarks.md from main.

main README line 17 advertises the production fork TheTom/llama-cpp-turboquant as targeting 'Metal, CUDA, HIP, CPU', and upstream llama.cpp merged fast WHT kernels on CPU (PR #22631). The reading never checks whether a CPU turbo3/turbo4 kernel actually exists, which is the decisive feasibility fact for a CPU-only town (and would make seed 5 concrete rather than speculative).
No license check anywhere. LICENSE on main is Apache 2.0; reusable_assets are recommended without terms. Sibling readings (orcabonsai) did check licenses.

The reading is silent on the town's vision 3 (two or more cooperating tiny models) and the owner's spiking / coupled-oscillator / neuron-as-byte threads; every seed is KV-quantization throughput on one model. Nothing connects this source to the owner's stated threads.
'qwen3.8 50b' is left unresolved, but the sibling trove source bonsai2-small-gpu references a 'qwen 3.8 mtp head grafted back'; the reader does not cross-reference the trove.

The repo's own papers argue the evaluation oracle is wrong for this exact comparison: why-mse-fails-for-kv-quantization.md says MSE is adversarial for KV quality and KLD should be tracked, and docs/papers/attn-rotation-and-ppl-artifact.md says corpus PPL can rank KV configs backwards. Every seed falsifier in the reading uses PPL or tokens/s; the oracle risk is never flagged.

Energy / tokens-per-Joule is listed as absent but no measurement path is proposed (powermetrics on Metal, nvidia-smi on CUDA, RAPL on the ARM box) even though the town's moral is knowledge-per-token-spent.
strongest_seed: Seed 5 (block-32 + graph-side-WHT + pre-rotate-queries is vendor-portable; on the 4-core ARM CPU with a <=2B Qwen3.5 model, turbo3 KV decode is >=0.85x q8_0 tokens/s so 4.6x-smaller KV costs no speed). It is the only seed measured on the town's actual hardware class, is cheap and local (~30-60 min, 0 USD), has zero CPU evidence in the source so either outcome is genuinely new, and both outcomes are decision-relevant: a pass unlocks 4.6x KV savings on ordinary RAM, a fail kills the CPU deployment path. Caveat: it requires a CPU turbo kernel, and main README's claim that the fork has a CPU backend is unverified.
weakest_seed: Seed 4 (a <=2B draft model sharing the same turbo3 KV cache recovers the decode gap via speculative decoding). It invents a shared-KV draft/target architecture that appears nowhere in the source, its proposed 'CPU validation' with llama.cpp --model-draft does not test the claimed dequant-amortization mechanism, and main's own dflash-self-draft paper already reports a ~1.33x architectural ceiling on 75%-GDN hybrids plus infeasible consumer-hardware draft training. It is both under-evidenced and partially pre-empted, and it is GPU-throughput rather than CPU knowledge.
